newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada sees Montreal-Dorval cargo boost.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada sees Montreal-Dorval cargo boost.

text.p: This spring's shift of international passenger flights from Mirabel to Dorval airports will boost Montreal as an Air Canada Cargo gateway, a senior airline official said.

From May, intercontinental flights can use Dorval, Montreal's airport for U.S and domestic services. Most carriers are expected to move from remote, underutilized Mirabel, which handles only intercontinental flights, and will be left with passenger charters and freighters, industry sources added.

Almost since Mirabel was opened in 1975, Air Canada has operated only two daily transatlantic flights from Montreal - one to Paris, one to London - but the shift to Dorval, where intercontinental flights can connect with domestic and U.S. flights, has spurred it to add a daily flight to Frankfurt and two non-stops a week to Tel Aviv.

The Air Canada official said there is enormous interest is being expressed in the Frankfurt flights - particularly the two a week which will make an intermediate stop in Halifax, the lobster shipping capital of Atlantic Canada.

Air Canada Cargo will also use Dorval as a safety valve for its Toronto hub. If transatlantic flights to Toronto are full, freight can be put on flights to Dorval, and then put on a connecting flight to Toronto. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
